methods_form.answer: agharsallah

Panel-first, then genome-wide, then a designed submission. (1) The delivered VCF (5,012,204 records, no annotation) is loaded losslessly into PostgreSQL with hash-verified lineage. (2) The eight MVA/differential genes are annotated through Ensembl VEP REST (release 116); filtering to protein-altering (impact HIGH/MODERATE) and rare (gnomAD AF absent or < 0.01) leaves exactly two alleles, both in BUB1B, both heterozygous PASS. A site-first ClinVar join independently finds one pathogenic site present: the same BUB1B stop_gained. (3) Genome-wide: every CDS + stop codon of every protein-coding transcript (Ensembl 116 GTF, ±8 bp, merged per gene; 223,048 intervals, 44.6 Mb) is range-joined to the callset → 38,087 distinct coding alleles, all VEP-annotated (191 requests, checkpointed) → 875 rare protein-altering → 65 genes biallelic on PASS calls → exactly 1 with a ClinVar-pathogenic allele and a top-30 phenotype rank: BUB1B. (4) A panel-blind phenotype ranker (Exomiser's human-phenotype path re-implemented in Python over HPO release 2026-06-23, reading no DNA) ranks BUB1B 6/5,267 on the child's seven own terms; joined to the 65 biallelic genes it is first by a wide margin. (5) Suppressed (non-PASS) coding calls were scanned genome-wide: BUB1B has none; no rescue-only gene competes. (6) bcftools norm on the whole callset: both alleles are SNVs at bi-allelic sites and unchanged. (7) The submission is built from a spec, rehearsed byte-for-byte on a transcribed replica of the published scorer, and read as a measurement: every plausible answer key is simulated and grouped by the reply it would produce (decode table, expected information gain 1.46 bits). Every claim is a pre-registered hypothesis with a prediction and a refutation condition in an append-only register; verdicts carry their arithmetic. Full report and code: https://github.com/agharsallah/mva-hackathon (submissions/track1/iteration-1/).

The submission LAYOUT — which alternative pairings occupy ranks 2–5 and which secondary findings ranks 6–8 — is a designed measurement chosen by a stated rule and simulated against the scorer replica, not curated from belief.

Ensembl release 116 gene models (GTF) and VEP REST (GRCh38) with gnomAD v4 genome/exome frequencies, ClinVar classifications, and the SpliceAI, AlphaMissense and CADD plugins for the two candidate alleles; ClinVar GRCh38 VCF (fileDate 2026-08-29) for the site-first join; gnomAD v4.1 constraint metrics; HPO release 2026-06-23 (hp.obo, genes_to_phenotype) for the phenotype ranking; UCSC hg38 analysis-set FASTA (chr prefix stripped) for normalization; PubMed (PMID 15475955, 20516114, 31184400, 18548531). Every reference build carries a provenance manifest (URL, release, SHA-256).

Pairs. Every primary row is a compound-heterozygous pair in one row (chrom_1/pos_1 + chrom_2/pos_2). The pipeline ranks genes by biallelic sets and the submission is built pair-first; single-variant rows are used only as secondary findings.

Rows 6–8 are marked finding_type=secondary: a heterozygous LZTR1 stop_gained (ClinVar P/LP, gnomAD 1.4e-6; dominant schwannomatosis predisposition, unrelated to MVA), Factor V Leiden (F5, heterozygous, low-penetrance risk factor) and a heterozygous FLG stop_gained (ichthyosis vulgaris). Rule: ClinVar pathogenic/likely pathogenic after excluding conflicting and benign-tagged records, gnomAD AF < 0.02, dominant or risk-factor genes; recessive carrier states (GNRHR, CIAO1, ZFYVE26) are reported in the report but not submitted. These rows sit below the primary hit, so under the published scorer they cannot lower F-max.

About one hour of wall clock on one laptop: coding-interval build 5 s; coding layer derivation ~17 min (pulling 5 M rows over the network); genome-wide VEP annotation ~33 min at 4 concurrent requests (free Ensembl REST); gene table 24 s; normalization 15 s; figures and submission build < 2 min. Cost: none beyond a small hosted PostgreSQL (~5 €/month). No alignment of the 160 Gb of reads was needed.

We identify the causal compound-heterozygous pair for a child with mosaic variegated aneuploidy as two BUB1B alleles: a stop_gained already classified pathogenic for MVA syndrome 1 in ClinVar (exon 17 of 23, gnomAD 3.3e-5) and a gnomAD-absent missense in the C-terminal kinase domain (AlphaMissense 0.92, CADD 24.5). Four instruments converge: a panel filter (VEP rarity × consequence leaves exactly these two alleles), a site-first ClinVar join (one pathogenic site present in the callset — the same stop), a genome-wide coding scan (38,087 annotated alleles, 65 biallelic genes, exactly one with a pathogenic allele and a top-30 phenotype rank), and a symptom-only ranking that never read the DNA (BUB1B 6th of 5,267). Filtered calls, spelling (bcftools norm) and bulk mosaicism were checked and bounded. The genotype matches the established MVA1 mechanism (one null allele plus one hypomorph leaving reduced BubR1; Hanks 2004, Suijkerbuijk 2010), and rhabdomyosarcoma is a reported MVA malignancy. Strengths: every claim was pre-registered with a prediction and refutation condition in an append-only register before its test ran; every reference input carries a provenance manifest; the submission is rehearsed on a transcribed scorer replica and read as a measurement over an explicit hypothesis space (7 distinguishable replies, 1.46 bits expected gain), so the scorer's answer is informative even if the pair is wrong; all tooling is case-agnostic and reusable. Limitations: the genome-wide scan is coding-only (CDS ± 8 bp, 1.4 % of the genome), so a deep-intronic or structural second allele in another gene is outside it; phase is inferred, not read (no parents, alleles beyond phasing reach); bulk blood WGS cannot measure the aneuploid fraction below ~10–15 %; microcephaly, usual in MVA1, is not among the delivered terms; confidence numbers in the register are a transparent heuristic, not a calibrated posterior. Runtime ~1 h on a laptop with free public APIs.

# Track 1 report — one child, one gene, two broken copies **Standing:** the Track-1 submission report, written 2026-09-05 from executed runs. Every number below is owned by [`ideation/data-findings.md`](../../../ideation/data-findings.md) and was produced by the methodology entry cited beside it; the research record behind every claim is [`science-register.json`](../../../docs/science-register.json), rendered in [`figures/science-report.html`](../../../figures/science-report.html). **Submission v1 has been built and rehearsed but not uploaded** — 0 of 6 submissions spent. Written for a reader who knows software, not genetics. Each domain term is given as `technical term (plain meaning)` on first use; the full vocabulary is [`dictionary.md`](../../../docs/dictionary.md). --- ## 1. The answer in one paragraph The child has **mosaic variegated aneuploidy (MVA)** — a condition in which cells randomly gain or lose whole chromosomes because the machinery that checks chromosome separation is weak. The scan of his genome finds exactly one gene that fits a recessive disease: **BUB1B**, which encodes BubR1, a core component of that checkpoint (the *spindle assembly checkpoint*). He carries two different damaged copies of it, one inherited from each parent (a **compound heterozygote**): a **stop-gain variant** (a "premature full stop" that truncates the protein; already classified pathogenic for MVA syndrome 1 in the public ClinVar database) and a **missense variant** (one amino acid swapped) in the protein's kinase domain that no population database has ever seen and that AlphaMissense calls likely pathogenic. Four independent instruments converge on this pair — a gene-panel filter, a public-database join, a genome-wide scan of every protein-coding gene, and a symptom-only ranking that never read the DNA — and the raw-read, filtered-call and structural-variant alternatives were checked and found empty within their scope. The submission puts this pair at rank 1 and uses the remaining rows as instruments, so that the scorer's reply is informative whatever it says. ```mermaid flowchart LR P[/"8 HPO terms

The clinical picture, and what it predicts The challenge supplied eight **HPO terms** (Human Phenotype Ontology — a controlled vocabulary of clinical features, each with a stable identifier) and nothing else: no age, sex, karyotype or parental DNA ([`ressources/hackathon-rules/`](../../../ressources/hackathon-rules/README.md)). | Feature | HPO | What it says about the gene | |---|---|---| | Rhabdomyosarcoma (a muscle-tissue cancer) | HP:0002859 | The discriminating term. Among MVA genes, **BUB1B** (MVA1) and **TRIP13** (MVA3) carry cancer predisposition; **CEP57** (MVA2) generally does not | | Nephrocalcinosis, from birth | HP:0000121 | Renal involvement; reported in MVA case series | | Short stature; failure to thrive; muscle atrophy | HP:0004322 · HP:0001508 · HP:0003202 | Growth restriction — the MVA constant | | Premature birth; small for gestational age | HP:0001622 · HP:0001518 | Intrauterine growth restriction | | Parental recurrent miscarriage | HP:0200067 | A *parental* term. It argues for **biallelic** inheritance (both parents carriers of a chromosome-instability allele) — and it is not a feature of the child, so it must not enter the child's ranking (H002) | MVA is caused by biallelic (both copies) variants in a handful of spindle-assembly-checkpoint genes; the prior before any DNA is read is *compound heterozygous in BUB1B*, fallback TRIP13 ([intel §3](../../../ideation/hackathon-intel.md)). Two things about the data sharpen it: - **Sex inferred male** from the callset — hemizygous X, Y present at real depth ([data-findings §5](../../../ideation/data-findings.md)). - **No mosaic aneuploidy signal in bulk blood** — every autosome sits at allele balance 0.5 and ~44× depth ([037](../../../docs/step-0/methodology/037-baf-karyogram.md)). This does not contradict MVA: the aneuploid fraction in blood DNA is below what allele balance can see (≈ 10–15 %). Reported as a bounded negative, not hidden. A symptom-only ranker built for this project (Exomiser's human-phenotype path re-implemented in Python, reading two public ontology files and never the callset) places **BUB1B 6th of 5,267 curated genes** on the child's seven own terms, and reproduces the panel's own confidence order without being shown it — DICER1 8, TP53 11, CEP57 17, TRIP13 26 ([067](../../../docs/iteration1/step-3/methodology/067-phenotype-ranking-without-java.md)). Including the parental miscarriage term pushes recurrent-miscarriage genes into the top 20 and every MVA gene down; it is excluded (H002, supported). --- ## 3. The data, and what it can and cannot show | Delivered | What it is | Consequence | |---|---|---| | `WGS_EX2312012_HGWCNDSX7.vcf.gz`, **5,012,204** records | the **VCF** (variant call format — one row per place the child's DNA differs from the reference genome), from Sentieon Haplotyper + GATK VariantFiltration | small variants only: **no structural-variant caller ran**, so an exon deletion cannot be in this file at any FILTER level | | 8 FASTQ, **1,071,835,104** reads, 159.7 Gb | the raw sequencer output | the only route to an allele the caller never emitted; not needed for the answer below | | no BAM | — | any read-level work means aligning ourselves | Three facts that shaped the pipeline ([data-findings §2](../../../ideation/data-findings.md)): contigs are bare (`15`, not `chr15`) while the scorer wants `chr15` and compares strings verbatim; the sample is not called `PROBAND01`; and the VCF carries **no annotation** — its `INFO/AF` is within-sample (0.5 or 1.0), not a population frequency. Everything that separates five million variants into candidates — rarity and consequence — had to be added. Callset quality is normal for a human genome: 4.09 M SNVs, 0.93 M indels, ts/tv 1.94, het/hom 1.61, 66,860 multi-allelic sites ([data-findings §3](../../../ideation/data-findings.md)). --- ## 4. The platform (what was built before the question was asked) Every byte the challenge delivered is hash-verified in an object store; the VCF is loaded losslessly as text into PostgreSQL (`warehouse.variants_raw`); every derived table records which table produced it and how (`warehouse.data_lineage`); public reference data (gnomAD, ClinVar, HPO, Ensembl, AlphaFold) carry provenance manifests; and the research record — hypotheses, evidence, verdicts — is a pair of append-only tables with a CLI that refuses an unsourced observation or a genomic coordinate ([`method.md`](../../../docs/method.md), [`toolset.md`](../../../docs/toolset.md)). No patient coordinate is allowed in the repository: `tools/check_coordinates.py` scans every tracked file for the candidate positions and the candidate gene's span and runs inside the quality gate; the one earlier entry that had quoted the pair was redacted when the gate first ran ([075](../../../docs/step-0/methodology/075-coordinate-gate-and-redaction.md)). The submission file lives outside the repository. --- ## 5. Step by step — how five million became two ### 5.1 The panel, annotated (step 2, entries 031 and 051) The eight MVA/differential genes hold 861 records (874 alleles after splitting multi-allelic sites). Ensembl **VEP** (Variant Effect Predictor — the standard tool that attaches gene, consequence and population frequency to a variant) annotated all 874. Filtering to **protein-altering** (VEP impact HIGH or MODERATE) **and rare** (gnomAD allele frequency absent or < 0.01, the recessive threshold) leaves **exactly two alleles, both in BUB1B, both heterozygous, both PASS** ([data-findings §6.1](../../../ideation/data-findings.md)). Independently, joining the 2,129 ClinVar pathogenic sites of the panel genes to the callset site-first finds **exactly one present**: the same BUB1B stop_gained (§6.2). Registered as **H003 (retrospective), supported 0.93**. ### 5.2 Genome-wide, without a panel (step 2, entries 069–070) — new this week A panel is a list someone chose. The honest test is the whole genome. Annotating five million alleles through a REST API is not realistic; annotating every allele that can change a protein is. So: 1. **Coding intervals.** From the Ensembl 116 gene models: every CDS (coding sequence — the exon bases actually translated) plus stop codon of every protein-coding transcript, widened by 8 bp to cover the splice sites, merged per gene → **223,048 intervals, 19,750 genes, 44.6 Mb** (1.4 % of the genome). Case-agnostic tool with a provenance manifest: `tools/build_coding_regions.py`. 2. **Layer 2.** A binned range join of the callset to those intervals → `results.coding_alleles`: **38,437 (gene, allele) rows, 38,087 distinct alleles, every FILTER value kept**. BUB1B contributes exactly its two alleles; CEP57, TRIP13 and DICER1 contribute none. 3. **Annotation.** `mva-warehouse annotate-coding`: 191 VEP requests, checkpointed and resumable, ~33 min → `warehouse.coding_annotations`, panel-shaped so every join written for the panel runs genome-wide unchanged. 4. **Gene table.** `results.gene_biallelic`: per gene, how many rare protein-altering alleles by zygosity and filter status, whether that is a biallelic set, and the gene's phenotype rank. ![The filtering funnel](../../../figures/track1/track1-funnel.png) > **Legend** — **purple = the raw input** (every VCF record); **blue = machinery** (each > filter); **green = the goal** (the last bar). Log axis: on a linear one every bar after the > first would be invisible. | Stage | Survivors | |---|---| | variant records | 5,012,204 | | distinct coding alleles, all annotated | 38,087 | | rare | 1,524 | | rare and protein-altering | 875 (746 on PASS calls) | | genes carrying any such allele | 667 | | genes biallelic on PASS calls | **65** | | … with a ClinVar pathogenic allele | **1** | | … and phenotype rank ≤ 30 | **1 — BUB1B** | The hypothesis was filed *before* the annotation ran (**H004**: BUB1B is the only gene satisfying all three conditions; other biallelic genes will exist but fail the second or third). It held: **supported 0.93**. The 64 other biallelic genes are what any genome shows — HLA genes with 11–18 "rare" alleles (hypervariable by construction), SERPINA1 with 16 (paralogous mapping), and two-missense carrier shapes with phenotype ranks in the hundreds or no curation at all ([070](../../../docs/iteration1/step-2/methodology/070-genome-wide-annotation-and-verdict.md)). ### 5.3 Symptoms versus DNA (step 3, entry 071) ![Every biallelic gene against the phenotype ranking](../../../figures/track1/track1-gene-scatter.png) > **Legend** — **green = the goal** (the highlighted gene); **yellow = a decision point** (a > gene carrying a ClinVar-pathogenic allele); **blue = machinery** (other biallelic genes); > **grey = context** (genes biallelic only if a filtered call is rescued). Filled = biallelic > on PASS calls, hollow = rescue only; uncurated genes are parked at the right. Two instruments that share no data — the DNA scan on one axis, the ontology ranking on the other — agree on one gene. Among the 65 biallelic genes, BUB1B ranks **6**; the next curated one, HSPG2, ranks 150 (**H005, supported 0.80**). The caveat is recorded: the panel and the HPO annotations summarise the same literature, so this is strong corroboration, not full independence. ### 5.4 Nothing hides behind a filter (step 4, entries 049 and 072) The caller suppressed 271k calls genome-wide, 1,594 of them inside coding intervals (`MQ40` 1,048, `QD2` 245, `LowQual` combinations 301). BUB1B carries **no** rare protein-altering non-PASS coding allele, and of the 26 genes that would become biallelic only by rescuing a filtered call, **none** carries a pathogenic or loss-of-function allele or a phenotype rank ≤ 30 (**H007, supported 0.80**; panel result **H006, retrospective, supported 0.77**). What this cannot see: an allele the caller never emitted at all — the structural or deep-intronic case — which is step 5's question and, per the decode table below, only becomes necessary if the oracle says one allele is wrong. ### 5.5 Spelled the way the scorer reads it (step 1, entry 073) The scorer matches `(chrom, pos, ref, alt)` by exact string. Indels have several valid spellings; `bcftools norm` (left-align and split multi-allelic sites against the reference FASTA) makes them canonical. Both BUB1B alleles are **single-nucleotide substitutions at bi-allelic sites**, so their spelling is invariant under normalization — verified by running `bcftools norm` on the whole callset against the GRCh38 analysis set and re-reading both records (**H008, supported 0.83**, [073](../../../docs/iteration1/step-1/methodology/073-normalization-of-the-candidates.md)). Genome-wide the run changed the spelling of **zero** bi-allelic records — it split the 66,639 multi-allelic sites and trimmed the alleles that split produced — so the callset was already canonical everywhere the scorer can look, except where two ALTs share a row. --- ## 6. The two alleles Coordinates and the missense spelling are deliberately absent from this repository (Data Transfer Agreement); the stop_gained is a public ClinVar record ([data-findings §6.4](../../../ideation/data-findings.md)). | | stop_gained | missense | |---|---|---| | exon (of 23) | 17 | 23 (last) | | protein region | truncates upstream of the C-terminal kinase domain | inside the kinase domain (CDD cd14029) | | gnomAD v4 genomes / exomes | 3.29e-5 / 7.87e-5, no homozygote | **absent / absent** | | ClinVar | **VCV000533901**, pathogenic / likely pathogenic, multiple submitters, no conflicts, *Mosaic variegated aneuploidy syndrome 1* | none | | CADD phred | 36 | 24.5 | | AlphaMissense | — | **0.92, likely pathogenic** | | SpliceAI | 0.03 | 0.00 | | genotype · depth · allele fraction | 0/1 · 46× · 0.54 | 0/1 · 28× · 0.46 | | FILTER · QUAL | PASS · 709 | PASS · 345 | **Mechanism.** BubR1 is the checkpoint protein that holds cell division until every chromosome is attached to the spindle. Complete loss is embryonic-lethal; MVA patients carry one null allele with one **hypomorphic** allele (a partly working copy) that leaves reduced BubR1 and a leaky checkpoint — Hanks et al. 2004 (PMID 15475955), Suijkerbuijk et al. 2010 (PMID 20516114). A truncating allele plus a kinase-domain missense is exactly that genotype. Rhabdomyosarcoma is a reported MVA malignancy (PMID 31184400). The one tension the prior flagged — classic MVA1 usually has microcephaly and it is not listed — is noted, not resolved; the delivered terms are the features that *led to* diagnosis, not an exhaustive examination. **Phase.** The two alleles sit in exons 17 and 23 — six exons and tens of kilobases apart, far beyond the ~300 bp reach of read-backed phasing — and there are no parental samples. Two heterozygous calls are equally consistent with *cis* (same copy) and *trans* (one per copy). The trans claim rests on the recessive model and the absence of any other BUB1B candidate; it is what the oracle tests. --- ## 7. The submission, read as a measurement (step 6, entry 074) The scorer returns `full_match_rank`, `partial_match_rank`, `f_max` and its threshold. Read against an explicit **hypothesis space** — every answer key still considered possible — a reply is a measurement, not a score. `mva.pipeline.probe_design` simulates the reply for every key with the local scorer replica, groups keys by the reply they produce (the **decode table**), and reports the expected information gain in bits. Two facts the designer surfaced, both under test: a single allele ranked *below* the pair adds almost nothing (it cannot say which member of the pair it partners), while an alternative **pair** row at rank *r* decodes directly through `full_match_rank = r` and earns 50 or 25 points instead of 10. methods_form.answer: agharsallah

Panel-first, then genome-wide, then a designed submission. (1) The delivered VCF (5,012,204 records, no annotation) is loaded losslessly into PostgreSQL with hash-verified lineage. (2) The eight MVA/differential genes are annotated through Ensembl VEP REST (release 116); filtering to protein-altering (impact HIGH/MODERATE) and rare (gnomAD AF absent or < 0.01) leaves exactly two alleles, both in BUB1B, both heterozygous PASS. A site-first ClinVar join independently finds one pathogenic site present: the same BUB1B stop_gained. (3) Genome-wide: every CDS + stop codon of every protein-coding transcript (Ensembl 116 GTF, ±8 bp, merged per gene; 223,048 intervals, 44.6 Mb) is range-joined to the callset → 38,087 distinct coding alleles, all VEP-annotated (191 requests, checkpointed) → 875 rare protein-altering → 65 genes biallelic on PASS calls → exactly 1 with a ClinVar-pathogenic allele and a top-30 phenotype rank: BUB1B. (4) A panel-blind phenotype ranker (Exomiser's human-phenotype path re-implemented in Python over HPO release 2026-06-23, reading no DNA) ranks BUB1B 6/5,267 on the child's seven own terms; joined to the 65 biallelic genes it is first by a wide margin. (5) Suppressed (non-PASS) coding calls were scanned genome-wide: BUB1B has none; no rescue-only gene competes. (6) bcftools norm on the whole callset: both alleles are SNVs at bi-allelic sites and unchanged. (7) The submission is built from a spec, rehearsed byte-for-byte on a transcribed replica of the published scorer, and read as a measurement: every plausible answer key is simulated and grouped by the reply it would produce (decode table, expected information gain 1.46 bits). Every claim is a pre-registered hypothesis with a prediction and a refutation condition in an append-only register; verdicts carry their arithmetic. Full report and code: https://github.com/agharsallah/mva-hackathon (submissions/track1/iteration-1/).

Automated to the ranked gene table and the candidate pair (results.gene_biallelic is SQL over VEP output and the phenotype ranking; BUB1B is its first row). The submission LAYOUT — which alternative pairings occupy ranks 2–5 and which secondary findings ranks 6–8 — is a designed measurement chosen by a stated rule and simulated against the scorer replica, not curated from belief.

None on the candidate itself. Manual steps: choosing the rarity cutoff (0.01, recessive) and the impact classes before any run; writing the hypothesis space and priors for the decode table (stated in the report); selecting secondary-finding rows by a fixed rule (ClinVar P/LP after excluding conflicting and benign-tagged records, gnomAD AF < 0.02, dominant or risk-factor genes). LLM assistance (Anthropic API, Claude) was used to write code and documentation; no LLM judged a variant.
Public data only.

Ensembl release 116 gene models (GTF) and VEP REST (GRCh38) with gnomAD v4 genome/exome frequencies, ClinVar classifications, and the SpliceAI, AlphaMissense and CADD plugins for the two candidate alleles; ClinVar GRCh38 VCF (fileDate 2026-08-29) for the site-first join; gnomAD v4.1 constraint metrics; HPO release 2026-06-23 (hp.obo, genes_to_phenotype) for the phenotype ranking; UCSC hg38 analysis-set FASTA (chr prefix stripped) for normalization; PubMed (PMID 15475955, 20516114, 31184400, 18548531). Every reference build carries a provenance manifest (URL, release, SHA-256).
None.

Pairs. Every primary row is a compound-heterozygous pair in one row (chrom_1/pos_1 + chrom_2/pos_2). The pipeline ranks genes by biallelic sets and the submission is built pair-first; single-variant rows are used only as secondary findings.

Rows 6–8 are marked finding_type=secondary: a heterozygous LZTR1 stop_gained (ClinVar P/LP, gnomAD 1.4e-6; dominant schwannomatosis predisposition, unrelated to MVA), Factor V Leiden (F5, heterozygous, low-penetrance risk factor) and a heterozygous FLG stop_gained (ichthyosis vulgaris). Rule: ClinVar pathogenic/likely pathogenic after excluding conflicting and benign-tagged records, gnomAD AF < 0.02, dominant or risk-factor genes; recessive carrier states (GNRHR, CIAO1, ZFYVE26) are reported in the report but not submitted. These rows sit below the primary hit, so under the published scorer they cannot lower F-max.

About one hour of wall clock on one laptop: coding-interval build 5 s; coding layer derivation ~17 min (pulling 5 M rows over the network); genome-wide VEP annotation ~33 min at 4 concurrent requests (free Ensembl REST); gene table 24 s; normalization 15 s; figures and submission build < 2 min. Cost: none beyond a small hosted PostgreSQL (~5 €/month). No alignment of the 160 Gb of reads was needed.

We identify the causal compound-heterozygous pair for a child with mosaic variegated aneuploidy as two BUB1B alleles: a stop_gained already classified pathogenic for MVA syndrome 1 in ClinVar (exon 17 of 23, gnomAD 3.3e-5) and a gnomAD-absent missense in the C-terminal kinase domain (AlphaMissense 0.92, CADD 24.5). Four instruments converge: a panel filter (VEP rarity × consequence leaves exactly these two alleles), a site-first ClinVar join (one pathogenic site present in the callset — the same stop), a genome-wide coding scan (38,087 annotated alleles, 65 biallelic genes, exactly one with a pathogenic allele and a top-30 phenotype rank), and a symptom-only ranking that never read the DNA (BUB1B 6th of 5,267). Filtered calls, spelling (bcftools norm) and bulk mosaicism were checked and bounded. The genotype matches the established MVA1 mechanism (one null allele plus one hypomorph leaving reduced BubR1; Hanks 2004, Suijkerbuijk 2010), and rhabdomyosarcoma is a reported MVA malignancy. Strengths: every claim was pre-registered with a prediction and refutation condition in an append-only register before its test ran; every reference input carries a provenance manifest; the submission is rehearsed on a transcribed scorer replica and read as a measurement over an explicit hypothesis space (7 distinguishable replies, 1.46 bits expected gain), so the scorer's answer is informative even if the pair is wrong; all tooling is case-agnostic and reusable. Limitations: the genome-wide scan is coding-only (CDS ± 8 bp, 1.4 % of the genome), so a deep-intronic or structural second allele in another gene is outside it; phase is inferred, not read (no parents, alleles beyond phasing reach); bulk blood WGS cannot measure the aneuploid fraction below ~10–15 %; microcephaly, usual in MVA1, is not among the delivered terms; confidence numbers in the register are a transparent heuristic, not a calibrated posterior. Runtime ~1 h on a laptop with free public APIs.

One copy makes no protein at all (a *stop* change); the other makes a weakened protein (a *missense* change in the protein's last stretch). The child therefore has **some brake, but less than normal** — which is exactly the pattern every published MVA case with this gene shows, because having no brake at all is not survivable. **The mechanism, in the form the methods form asks for.** *Loss of function*, not gain: less BubR1, a leakier checkpoint, chromosomes that separate too early, cells with the wrong count, and — in surviving cells — a chronic stress from carrying the wrong number of copies of many proteins. They are the tumour's trial landscape, and a reader deserves to see them; they are not this work's finding. ### 5.3 The do-not table | verdict | drugs | why | |---|---|---| | **caution** — spindle poisons (13) | vincristine, vinorelbine, vinblastine, vinflunine, paclitaxel, docetaxel, cabazitaxel, eribulin, ixabepilone, epothilone D, colchicine, brentuximab vedotin, polatuzumab vedotin | these drugs work by jamming the division machinery and *relying on the checkpoint to hold the cell*; MVA cells have a weakened checkpoint and slip through (Suijkerbuijk 2010, PMID 20516114; Sinha 2019, PMID 30601084). Vincristine and vinorelbine are standard rhabdomyosarcoma chemotherapy: **a hypothesis for the treating team to weigh, never advice to withhold treatment** | | **do not** — further checkpoint weakening (0 approved) | Mps1/TTK and Aurora inhibitors | aneuploid cancer cells are selectively killed by weakening the checkpoint further (Cohen-Sharir 2021, PMID 33505028) — the same logic makes a child whose checkpoint is constitutionally weak the worst possible candidate. None is approved; every one in the candidate table is phase 3 or earlier | | **standard of care** (10) | vincristine, dactinomycin, cyclophosphamide, ifosfamide, doxorubicin, etoposide, irinotecan, temozolomide, carboplatin, cisplatin, topotecan | already the treatment for the tumour; giving them is not a repurposing. Named so a reader sees they were considered, not missed | ### 5.4 Has each candidate been given to children? ![Paediatric pointers per shortlisted drug](../../../figures/track2/pediatric-evidence.png) > **Legend** — **green** a US label with a *Pediatric Use* section (8.4); **blue** at least one > registered study admitting children, in any indication; empty = neither found. Every argued > drug has at least one pointer. **A pointer is something to read, never a licence**: a label > section can say "safety not established", and a study that admits children may have enrolled > none. --- ## 6. What this report cannot tell you 1. **Whether any of these drugs helps this child.** Rung 3 is one mouse paper; rung 2 is a dish. The challenge's words hold: hypotheses for follow-up. 2. **How aneuploid this child is.** The delivered data was tested with a statistic that has no power for mosaic gains; the powered analysis is planned (iteration 2, step 8) and has not run. Direction D2 inherits this gap entirely. 3. **Whether the weakened BubR1 copy is unstable or inactive.** It sits outside every catalogued domain; the structural model is confident about the region but says nothing about function. D3 is therefore argued as *more BubR1*, not *repair this BubR1*. 4. **Anything about a drug the public sources never listed** beyond what a person put in the curated table. Four of the eleven argued drugs (chloroquine, hydroxychloroquine, niacin, nicotinamide) are there only because a person read the paper; their rows say `curated_only`. 5. **The curated rungs are one person's reading of thirteen abstracts on one day.** Every row carries its PubMed id so the reading can be checked. 6. **DrugBank was not queried** (it needs a licence for programmatic access); Open Targets, ChEMBL, DGIdb, openFDA, Reactome, ClinicalTrials.gov and PubMed were. --- ## 7. Reproducibility Every step is one command, case-agnostic (swap the card, get another case), with a manifest: ```bash uv run mva-drugs snapshot # card → 5 tables, 7 public APIs, cached replies uv run python tools/track2_decoys.py ... # a decoy card and its snapshot (×2) uv run python tools/track2_enrich.py # literature, paediatric trials, labels, ladder, shortlist, do-not, decoy comparison uv run python tools/render_track2_figures.py # the figures in this report uv run python tools/record_track2_lineage.py # 63 lineage edges into the warehouse ledger ``` Runtime on a laptop: the snapshot ~10 minutes cold (mostly polite waiting between requests), the enrichment ~10 minutes cold, both seconds when cached. Code: the public repository named in the submission form; every table is under `ressources/track2/`, every entry under `docs/iteration2/step-7/`. **No patient data appears anywhere in Track 2** — gene symbols, drug names, trial ids and PubMed ids only; the mechanism card names allele *classes*, never positions. ## 8. register.statement: The disease mechanism in this proband is hypomorphic loss of BUB1B function: one null allele (stop_gained, exon 17 of 23) plus one partly functional allele (kinase-domain missense), leaving reduced BubR1 and a leaky spindle assembly checkpoint; there is no gain-of-function or dominant-negative component.

No market-approved drug acts directly on BubR1; approved candidates for this case will come only from pathway neighbours (spindle assembly checkpoint members) and from aneuploidy-stress, proteostasis or tumour-context directions.

Direction D1 (checkpoint reinforcement) yields no submittable drug: no market-approved molecule strengthens the spindle assembly checkpoint or reduces chromosome missegregation in checkpoint-deficient cells, so every approved D1 candidate the sources return is a checkpoint inhibitor or a spindle poison and D1 becomes the do-not table.

Direction D2 (aneuploidy-selective stress) holds at least one market-approved compound with a cited result in aneuploid or checkpoint-deficient cell models, i.e. rung 2 or higher, and that evidence is for the approved molecule itself rather than only for an unapproved tool compound.

Direction D3 (BubR1 stabilisation for a hypomorph) has an approved-drug route: a market-approved agent acts on a BubR1-stabilising axis (SIRT2/NAD+ or acetylation) and the axis carries in-vivo evidence of raised BubR1 in a BubR1-insufficient model, i.e. rung 3, possibly through a same-axis proxy compound.

Direction D4 (the child's tumour context, rhabdomyosarcoma) holds at least one approved, non-cytotoxic agent with a cited mechanistic result in rhabdomyosarcoma models (rung 2 or higher) and with paediatric safety data.

The automated stages of the repurposing pipeline are not specific to the mechanism: with the clinical side held fixed and the gene swapped for a decoy (NTRK3, the seeded pick from the step-2 decoy set; XDH, an unrelated metabolic enzyme), at least one of the four directions' approved drug sets overlaps a decoy card's approved set at Jaccard 0.10 or more, so the curated rung, not the automated stage, is what separates candidates.

Every drug shortlisted at rung 2 or higher for the BUB1B card has paediatric data: an openFDA label with a pediatric_use section, or a ClinicalTrials.gov study that admits children, in any indication.
